events.title: Joan of Arc is canonized
events.shortBlurb: Nearly five centuries after she was burned as a heretic, the Maid of Orléans was raised to the altars…
body: Burned as a heretic in the Old Market square of Rouen on 30 May 1431, at nineteen years of age, after a trial presided over by Bishop Pierre Cauchon, Joan of Arc had been dead nearly five centuries when Pope Benedict XV solemnly canonized her in St. Peter's Basilica on 16 May 1920.

Her condemnation had in fact been reversed long before: at the rehabilitation trial of 1455 and 1456, authorized by Pope Callixtus III at the petition of her family, the judgment of Rouen was annulled as iniquitous, and her innocence solemnly declared before the whole Church.

Beatified by Pope Pius X in 1909 and canonized amid the thanksgiving that followed the First World War, she was declared a patroness of France by Pope Pius XI in 1922 — the girl an ecclesiastical court had condemned as a heretic and relapsed now venerated by the whole Church as a virgin.

sources.text: Vatican, Canonization of St. Joan of Arc (vatican.va)
